items.readable_text:
Content:
In this topic, we'll learn how to compute the surface area of solids formed by gluing prisms or cylinders along congruent faces. This is useful in real-world settings, for example, estimating materials, cost, or coverage (paint/wrap) when separate pieces are joined.

Content:
For instance, consider two identical cubes with a side length of [MATH: 1] meter.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/588cc2f0ae447c3a94569f61d26d02d8]

Content:
Suppose the cubes are joined together by gluing one of their square faces together, as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/459c67eeaeba85f77b4b8c2015a737ef]

Content:
Let's find the surface area, in square meters, of the combined solid.

Content:
If [MATH: s] denotes the side length of a cube, then its surface area is given by
[MATH: S|= 6 ⋅ (face area); = 6 ⋅ s^{2}; = 6s^{2}.]

Content:
Therefore, the surface area of a single cube of side length [MATH: s=1\,\textrm m] (before joining them) is
[MATH: S|= 6(1)^{2}; = 6 ⋅ 1; = 6m^{2}.]

Content:
This means that the surface areas of both cubes (before joining) is
[MATH: 2S = 2\cdot 6 = 12\,\textrm{m}^2.]

Content:
When the two cubes are glued together at their square faces, one face from each is hidden. In other words, a total of two square faces are hidden. This reduces the total surface area by
[MATH: 2s^2=2(1)^2 = 2\,\textrm{m}^2.]
Therefore, the surface area of the combined solid is

Content:
[MATH: 2S − 2s^{2}|= 12 − 2; = 10m^{2}.]

items.title: Finding the Combined Surface Area of Two Cubes

sections.normalized_html: Two identical cubes have a side length of [MATH: 4] meters. The cubes are joined together by gluing one of their square faces together. Find the surface area, in square meters, of the combined solid.
sections.readable_text: Two identical cubes have a side length of [MATH: 4] meters. The cubes are joined together by gluing one of their square faces together. Find the surface area, in square meters, of the combined solid.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
If [MATH: s] denotes the side length of a cube, then its surface area is given by [MATH: S|= 6 ⋅ (face area); = 6 ⋅ s^{2}; = 6s^{2}.]

Therefore, the surface area of a single cube of side length [MATH: s=4\,\textrm m] (before joining them) is [MATH: S|= 6(4)^{2}; = 6 ⋅ 16; = 96m^{2}.]

This means that the surface areas of both cubes (before joining) is [MATH: 2S = 2\cdot 96 = 192\,\textrm{m}^2.]

When the two cubes are glued together at their square faces, one face from each is hidden, reducing the total surface area by [MATH: 2s^2=2(4)^2 = 32\,\textrm{m}^2.] Therefore, the surface area of the combined solid is

[MATH: 2S − 2s^{2}|= 192 − 32; = 160m^{2}.]

sections.normalized_html: A square-based right rectangular prism has a height of [MATH: h] and a base side length of [MATH: s.] The second right rectangular prism has an identical square base but is nine times higher. The two prisms are joined together by gluing one of their square bases together. Construct an expression that gives the surface area of the combined solid.
sections.readable_text: A square-based right rectangular prism has a height of [MATH: h] and a base side length of [MATH: s.] The second right rectangular prism has an identical square base but is nine times higher. The two prisms are joined together by gluing one of their square bases together. Construct an expression that gives the surface area of the combined solid.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
We are given that

  • the first prism has a base side length of [MATH: s] and a height of [MATH: h,] while

  • the second prism has a base's side length of [MATH: s] and a height of [MATH: 9h.]

So, the surface area of the first prism is given by [MATH: S_{1}|= 2 ⋅ (base area) + 4 ⋅ (lateral surface area); = 2 ⋅ s^{2} + 4 ⋅ sh; = 2s^{2} + 4sh.]

And the surface area of the second prism is given by [MATH: S_{2}|= 2 ⋅ (base area) + 4 ⋅ (lateral surface area); = 2 ⋅ s^{2} + 4 ⋅ s ⋅ 9h; = 2s^{2} + 36sh.]

When the two prisms are glued together at their square bases, one base from each is hidden, reducing the total surface area by [MATH: 2s^2.] Therefore, the surface area of the combined solid is [MATH: S_{1} + S_{2} − 2s^{2}|= (2s^{2} + 4sh) + (2s^{2} + 36sh) − 2s^{2}; = 4s^{2} + 40sh − 2s^{2}; = 2s^{2} + 40sh.]

Hint: You may use the fact that the surface area [MATH: S] of a cylinder is given by [MATH: S|= 2 ⋅ (base area) + (lateral surface area); = 2 ⋅ πr^{2} + 2πrh] where [MATH: r] is the base radius and [MATH: h] is its height.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
In this topic, we'll learn how to compute the surface area of solids formed by gluing prisms or cylinders along congruent faces. This is useful in real-world settings, for example, estimating materials, cost, or coverage (paint/wrap) when separate pieces are joined.

Content:
For instance, consider two identical cubes with a side length of [MATH: 1] meter.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/588cc2f0ae447c3a94569f61d26d02d8]

Content:
Suppose the cubes are joined together by gluing one of their square faces together, as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/459c67eeaeba85f77b4b8c2015a737ef]

Content:
Let's find the surface area, in square meters, of the combined solid.

Content:
If [MATH: s] denotes the side length of a cube, then its surface area is given by
[MATH: S|= 6 ⋅ (face area); = 6 ⋅ s^{2}; = 6s^{2}.]

Content:
Therefore, the surface area of a single cube of side length [MATH: s=1\,\textrm m] (before joining them) is
[MATH: S|= 6(1)^{2}; = 6 ⋅ 1; = 6m^{2}.]

Content:
This means that the surface areas of both cubes (before joining) is
[MATH: 2S = 2\cdot 6 = 12\,\textrm{m}^2.]

Content:
When the two cubes are glued together at their square faces, one face from each is hidden. In other words, a total of two square faces are hidden. This reduces the total surface area by
[MATH: 2s^2=2(1)^2 = 2\,\textrm{m}^2.]
Therefore, the surface area of the combined solid is

Content:
[MATH: 2S − 2s^{2}|= 12 − 2; = 10m^{2}.]

---

Item 2 — Example: Finding the Combined Surface Area of Two Cubes

Example Prompt:
Two identical cubes have a side length of [MATH: 4] meters. The cubes are joined together by gluing one of their square faces together. Find the surface area, in square meters, of the combined solid.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
If [MATH: s] denotes the side length of a cube, then its surface area is given by
[MATH: S|= 6 ⋅ (face area); = 6 ⋅ s^{2}; = 6s^{2}.]

Therefore, the surface area of a single cube of side length [MATH: s=4\,\textrm m] (before joining them) is
[MATH: S|= 6(4)^{2}; = 6 ⋅ 16; = 96m^{2}.]

This means that the surface areas of both cubes (before joining) is
[MATH: 2S = 2\cdot 96 = 192\,\textrm{m}^2.]

When the two cubes are glued together at their square faces, one face from each is hidden, reducing the total surface area by
[MATH: 2s^2=2(4)^2 = 32\,\textrm{m}^2.]
Therefore, the surface area of the combined solid is

[MATH: 2S − 2s^{2}|= 192 − 32; = 160m^{2}.]

[MATH: S_{1}|= 2 ⋅ (base area) + 4 ⋅ (lateral surface area); = 2 ⋅ s^{2} + 4 ⋅ sh; = 2s^{2} + 4sh.]

When the two prisms are glued together at their square bases, one base from each is hidden, reducing the total surface area by [MATH: 2s^2.] Therefore, the surface area of the combined solid is
[MATH: S_{1} + S_{2} − 2s^{2}|= (2s^{2} + 4sh) + (2s^{2} + 36sh) − 2s^{2}; = 4s^{2} + 40sh − 2s^{2}; = 2s^{2} + 40sh.]
